headword: {国民主権|こくみんしゅけん}
gloss: popular sovereignty; sovereignty of the people

definitions.explanation: The principle that political power ultimately belongs to the people of a nation; one of the three basic principles of the Constitution of Japan.

examples.japanese: {国民主権|こくみんしゅけん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{原則|げんそく}→原則：11801_gensoku⟧。
⟦{日本国憲法|にほんこくけんぽう}→日本国憲法：31842_nihonkokukenpou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{国民主権|こくみんしゅけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{定|さだ}めている→定める：10448_sadameru⟧。
examples.english: The Constitution of Japan establishes popular sovereignty.

examples.japanese: {国民主権|こくみんしゅけん}、⟦{基本的人権|きほんてきじんけん}→基本的人権：33199_kihontekijinken⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{尊重|そんちょう}→尊重：03327_sonchou⟧、⟦{平和主義|へいわしゅぎ}→平和主義：31402_heiwashugi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{憲法|けんぽう}→憲法：02744_kenpou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{三大原則|さんだいげんそく}だ。
examples.english: Popular sovereignty, respect for fundamental human rights and pacifism are the three main principles of the constitution.

notes:
Taught in Japanese schools as one of the three principles of the 1947 constitution. The Meiji constitution before it placed sovereignty in the emperor ({天皇主権|てんのうしゅけん}).
